openings.claim: Tighter fit may restrain motion while friction or clamp rocking makes exchanged seating history-dependent. Seat each rod against fixed corner contacts and an end stop before hand-tightening its captive closing bar. Join two independently releasable plywood seats inside the envelope; supplied bolts/nuts form bars/stops; cord and elastic loops retain every released component.
openings.discriminator: If seating history dominates, corner seating should lower unloaded return error despite insertion clearance. The clearance-dominance rival predicts tighter surrounding contact gives smaller loaded displacement without worse return error. These competing predictions are unmeasured; the two supplied trials establish neither explanation.
openings.probe: Reuse supplied materials for at most two configurations: corner seating then closure versus tighter surrounding contact. Each gets twelve timed exchanges: five of each original rod, then 18 mm substitution for the last two. Log every return; keep base/pointer attachment unchanged. Run four ten-second 10 N load trials after exchanges 5, 10, 11, 12. Reject if unloaded return or loaded position leaves the 2 mm circle, any exchange reaches forty seconds, or retention fails. Exceeding 100 fabrication minutes or twenty testing minutes defeats probe capacity; caps establish no feasibility.
openings.uncertainty: Six plywood pieces/eight bolts may realize both seats, stops and retention within a 90 mm cube; bolt lengths/frame geometry are unspecified. Hand-tightening restraint without rod damage is unproven; force/friction unknown. Corner referencing may preserve the pointer datum across widths; 18 mm substitution can defeat this premise. No drilling, adhesive or permanent rod marks; hand-operated assembly/adjustment only; no component may fall free.

lineage.reason: Retains causal relation, rival predictions, defeat conditions, resource caveats and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Retain one discriminating probe. Fabrication, stiffness and substitution compatibility remain unproven; requirements are acceptance conditions, with no deployment claim.
